transcript.content: Hello. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic, and how can I help you?

I've been feeling deeply depressed and so sad for several months now, and it feels like I can't get out of this dark place. On top of that, I've been hearing voices and experiencing other distressing things for over a year. I just really need some help finding my way out of this.

You mentioned hearing voices for over a year, but feeling depressed for only several months. Was there a period of at least two weeks during this past year when you heard these voices but did not feel depressed?

Yes, absolutely. The voices actually started over a year ago, and for the first several months, I wasn't feeling down or depressed at all. The heavy sadness and depression didn't set in until much later on.
During these past several months of feeling depressed, have you also experienced other symptoms like changes in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

I've almost completely lost my appetite lately, and I just don't care about any of the hobbies or things I used to enjoy anymore. My sleep and energy levels seem about the same as usual, though. It just feels like there is no pleasure in anything.
During these past several months of feeling down, have you also struggled with feelings of worthlessness, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of death?

No, I haven't really struggled with feeling worthless, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of death. Instead, it's just this constant, heavy sadness and a feeling of complete emptiness and emotional numbness.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) and Schizophrenia. During the interview, the patient clarified that although they have experienced depressive symptoms for several months, these symptoms do not meet the diagnostic threshold for a Major Depressive Episode (only 3 symptoms are present: depressed mood, anhedonia, and decreased appetite, with no changes in sleep, energy, worthlessness, concentration, or suicidal ideation). Because a full major mood episode is required to diagnose Schizoaffective Disorder, this candidate is ruled out, leaving Schizophrenia as the most accurate diagnosis.

candidates: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
inference_history.note: The patient presents with both chronic psychotic symptoms (hearing voices for over a year) and depressive symptoms (feeling deeply depressed for several months). Because the psychotic symptoms appear to have a longer duration than the depressive episode, Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) and Schizophrenia with depressive features are strong candidates. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is also included as a differential, though it typically requires psychotic symptoms to occur exclusively during the depressive episode.
